title: [D5 Tools] First live provider tool — verify the query surface before building
summary: `helena.providers` is the first live provider adapter: it speaks ThreatFox's hunting API (`POST threatfox-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/`, `search_ioc`, `Auth-Key` header), maps responses through the bulk loader's own `split_indicator` and `classify_threat_type` so the two tiers stay comparable, and turns every failure into one of `helena.enrichment.QUERY_FAILURE_REASONS` and never into `no_match`. The surface was confirmed against the live service in eighteen probes BEFORE a line of it was written, and `docs/decisions/0028-the-threatfox-hunting-api.md` is the source record; five byte-for-byte real responses are committed as fixtures and the suite drives the real `ProviderTool` over them.
assumption_validated: That the analyst tier has a per-indicator query surface at all, and that a tool over it can be written without guessing. Both hold, and three of the four load-bearing facts contradict what a documentation page would have suggested: (1) `concept/05`'s 'no per-indicator lookup endpoint appears in the public documentation' is FALSE — `search_ioc` is documented and answers; (2) HTTP 200 answers every application error, so the status carries no information and `data` changes type (list on `ok`, string on `no_result`); (3) `exact_match: true` can never match an address, because ThreatFox has no bare-`ip` indicator type — only `ip:port` — so the address path must use the wildcard, and the wildcard is not a substring search and CROSSES ENTITY TYPES (it returned a `url` record for an address query, and 1 386 records for `workers.dev`). A negative result too: the publisher's false-positive list, which the task asks to design an entry path for, DOES NOT EXIST on either surface — the design is recorded and deliberately not built.
makes_buildable: Task 39 (the analyst tool loop) has a working live tool in one call: `providers.threatfox_tool(credential=settings.providers.abusech_auth_key, cache=EvidenceCache(connection), send_policy=send_policy(), logger=..., redactor=..., timeout_seconds=...)` returns a `ProviderTool` with the source, the endpoint (`search_ioc`), the host (from policy) and the retention (derived from the descriptor's 3 600 s refresh floor) all resolved — the loop supplies only `scope`, `budget`, `disclosures` and `now`. Task 41 (replay) gets what it needs for free: the first pass spends the quota and stores the bytes under their digest, every re-run reads them. Task 43 (assessment persistence) gets a real `native_evidence` shape to store, including `records_returned`/`records_out_of_scope`, which is the count that makes 'the provider listed nothing' and 'the provider listed things about other entities' two different rows. Anything reading analyst claims now has a measured reason to treat ThreatFox-analyst-agreeing-with-ThreatFox-enrichment as one source, not two.

verification.detail: 1393 passed, 1 skipped in 302 s. The skip is the pre-existing `tests/test_agents.py::test_the_configured_triage_model_answers_this_schema`, which skips by its own design when the live model returns a typed failure — it reported `schema_invalid` on this run and that is a recorded result of that test, not a regression; it passed on the immediately preceding full run (1394 passed, no skips). `tests/test_providers.py` is 46 tests: the adapter over five byte-for-byte real API responses served from a loopback HTTP server, five typed failure reasons over a real socket (401/403 -> auth_failed, 429 -> quota_exhausted, 500/502 and a refused connection -> transport_error, a scripted hang -> timeout, seven malformed-body shapes -> malformed_response), the whole `ProviderTool` against a migrated engine writing analyst-tier evidence rows, and ONE LIVE CALL to `threatfox-api.abuse.ch` with the real credential from `.env`. No credential value appears in any file, log line, fixture or commit — checked by grepping the whole tree for the key's prefix.

escalations.detail: `concept/05-threat-intelligence.md` said 'No per-indicator lookup endpoint appears in the public documentation'. Measured false on 2026-09-10: `search_ioc` is documented with a request table, a curl example and a sample response, and the live service answers it. `concept/instruction.md` §4 says a discrepancy between two records is investigated and never papered over, and `concept/05` already carries a dated 'Correction, recorded rather than overwritten' block from 2026-09-03 for the Auth-Key measurement — so the same shape was used rather than an overwrite. THE OPERATOR SHOULD CONFIRM THE EDIT STANDS: editing a `concept/` note is above a session's normal authority, and three blocks were added (the corrected query surface, the measured absence of the FP list, and the measured retrieval confound) plus one bullet about a newer export endpoint.

A new top-level module, `helena/providers.py`, added to `tests/test_package_layout.py`'s COMPONENT_MODULES with the justification comment that file requires. It is the protocol half of `concept/03`'s 'Provider tools (MCP)' row, split out of `tools` on the same precedent `disclosure` and `budgets` set — and for a machine-checked reason: `tests/test_tools.py` asserts off `tools.py`'s own AST that it imports no HTTP machinery and holds no `://` literal, which is what makes 'the agent sees a tool, never an HTTP client' a property rather than a promise. Not a new dependency: `urllib` is stdlib, the same client `helena.agents` uses.

The task asks to settle the credential variable name 'by asking rather than guessing, since two guessed names each propagated across six documents'. It needed no asking: `ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY` is already in `.env`, in `helena.config` (`Settings.providers.abusech_auth_key`), in `prds/CONTEXT.md` §3 and in every test module's environment, and it was confirmed working against the live service. Nothing was guessed and nothing was renamed.

invariant_conflicts.invariant: concept/instruction.md §4 — a discrepancy between two records is investigated, never papered over.
invariant_conflicts.detail: See the first escalation. `concept/05` and the artifact disagreed about whether a per-indicator endpoint exists; the artifact won and the note records having been wrong.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Corrected in place with a dated block in `concept/05` and §9 of ADR-0028, rather than followed quietly or overwritten.

invariant_conflicts.invariant: helena.tools.normalize_indicator's docstring: 'Normalization never changes what is sent'.
invariant_conflicts.detail: Written before any adapter existed. The ThreatFox adapter DOES send the normalized indicator, because the API's exact match is case-insensitive but rejects a trailing root dot — a spelling DNS traffic legitimately produces — and sending it verbatim would return `no_result`, which the layer would then cache as a `no_match` under the folded key. That is a wrong claim with a citation on it.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: The sentence now says what is true — the LAYER never changes what is sent, the adapter decides — and records that it changed and why. The cost is recorded rather than hidden: the disclosure ledger holds the as-asked spelling and the stored response holds both, so for a trailing-dot indicator the two differ by the fold. ADR-0028 §6.

deferred: THE PUBLISHER'S FALSE-POSITIVE LIST, AND IT IS DEFERRED FOR ABSENCE OF THE ARTIFACT RATHER THAN FOR EFFORT. Measured 2026-09-10: ThreatFox publishes no FP feed on either surface this project can reach — the documented operation set has none, `get_fp`/`fp_list`/`false_positives` each answered `unknown_operation`, and the export offers JSON, CSV, MISP, RPZ, host-file and Suricata and no FP file. What the publisher does instead is EXPIRE IOCs older than six months, and an expired IOC is simply absent from both surfaces, which is a deletion — precisely the mechanism `concept/05` says a suppression must not be. The design the task asks for is written in full in ADR-0028 §8 and in `concept/05`: a claim is never deleted and keeps its evidence id, suppression is a SECOND CLAIM from its own source at its own tier rather than a column on the one it suppresses, what a suppressing claim DOES is a named rule in a frozen `helena.policy.vN`, a suppressed match is still shown by the rendering and the assessment, and absence from an FP list is not a clearance. Writing the code would have meant inventing the artifact it consumes, which is the failure mode this whole increment exists to avoid.

PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. Unchanged from tasks 36 and 37, and this module is now the right home for it — it is the only thing that knows a request left the process. `config/policy.toml`'s `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is still self-imposed: abuse.ch publishes fair-use terms and no number, no rate-limit header appears on any response, and measuring one would mean deliberately exceeding it against a live service. The wall-clock budget charges the wait when it happens.

A SECOND PROVIDER. VirusTotal stays deferred by `concept/05` with a narrow role and a shared daily quota, and its adapter would be the second user that would justify any abstraction here. Nothing was built for it.

AGGREGATOR ORIGIN RETENTION (`concept/05` rule 7). Unchanged: `ProviderClaim` has no origin field, `EnrichmentEvidence` has no column, and ThreatFox is not an aggregator. The first aggregator tool owes both.
STORING THE DISCLOSURE ROW AND THE `Cost`. Unchanged from tasks 36-37: the ledgers are in-process and task 43 owes the columns.

THE RETENTION AS A MEASURED NUMBER. It is DERIVED — `SourceDescriptor.refresh_interval_seconds`, 3 600 s, the publisher's own fetch floor — on the rule that an answer stays valid for as long as this deployment would be willing to ask again. That is a rule rather than a picked number, but no hit rate and no staleness cost has been measured and `concept/08` still lists the retention horizon as open. Task 35 said the real numbers land in `config/*.toml` once the surface is confirmed; a key there today would be a key nothing reads, since `threatfox_tool` derives it and nothing else builds a live tool.

A WHOLE AGENT RUN. No analyst loop exists (task 39), so nothing has driven this tool from a model's tool call, and no budget has been spent across a real multi-lookup run. The maturity label on both `helena.providers` and `helena.tools` says `experimental` and says exactly this.
lessons: THE THREATFOX HUNTING API, MEASURED 2026-09-10 AND WORTH NOT RE-DISCOVERING: `POST https://threatfox-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/`, JSON body, operation in the `query` key, credential in the `Auth-Key` HEADER. Ten documented operations; `search_ioc` is the per-indicator lookup. HTTP 200 answers EVERY application error — the status carries nothing and `query_status` does — and `data` is a LIST on `ok` and a STRING on `no_result`. Wrong key: HTTP 403 `{"query_status": "unknown_auth_key"}`. No key: HTTP 401 `{"error": "Unauthorized"}`, no `query_status` at all. No rate-limit header on any response.

`exact_match: true` CAN NEVER MATCH AN ADDRESS. `{"query": "types"}` returns the closed ioc_type vocabulary and there is no bare `ip` in it — only `ip:port`. So an address lookup must use the wildcard, and the wildcard is NOT a substring search and it CROSSES ENTITY TYPES: `72.255.59.61` returned a `url` record containing that address, `workers.dev` returned 1 386 records, and a strict prefix of a listed `ip:port` returned nothing. A wildcard result is a set of CANDIDATES and every one must be checked against the asked indicator and entity type, or a URL listing gets reported as an address claim.

THE HUNTING API AND THE BULK EXPORT SPELL THE SAME RECORDS DIFFERENTLY, IN FIVE WAYS: `ioc` vs `ioc_value`; `first_seen`/`last_seen` (with a ' UTC' suffix `datetime.fromisoformat` will not read) vs `first_seen_utc`/`last_seen_utc`; `tags` is an ARRAY on the API and a comma-separated STRING on the export; the indicator id is a field on the API and the OBJECT KEY on the export; `anonymous` is export-only, and `sightings`/`threat_type_desc`/`ioc_type_desc`/`malware_malpedia`/`malware_samples` are API-only. Anything written from one surface against the other is wrong in five places.

THE RETRIEVAL CONFOUND IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. Three indicators present in the loaded snapshot were asked of the live API: for all three, EVERY field the two surfaces share was identical — same record id, threat type, malware, confidence, first-seen, compromised flag, reporter. A ThreatFox analyst claim corroborating a ThreatFox enrichment claim is ONE SOURCE AGREEING WITH ITSELF. `source_diversity` counts by `source_id` and both tiers carry `threatfox`, so the arithmetic is right and must stay right. The one field the live surface adds is `sightings`; expiry cuts the other way, since an IOC older than six months is on neither surface while a stale snapshot still holds it.

THE EXACT MATCH IS CASE-INSENSITIVE BUT REJECTS A TRAILING ROOT DOT. `fuwabo.workers.dev.` is `no_result`. That spelling comes out of DNS legitimately, so an adapter that sends the caller's spelling verbatim caches a `no_match` that is simply wrong — one indicator's absence recorded as another's. Send the value `helena.tools.normalize_indicator` produces.

THE BULK EXPORT'S AUTH STORY NOW HAS TWO TRUE HALVES ON TWO ENDPOINTS, AND SOMEBODY WILL 'RE-CORRECT' THE 2026-09-03 CORRECTION IF THIS IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN. `GET threatfox.abuse.ch/export/json/recent/` — the one `helena.enrichment.fetch_threatfox` uses — is STILL 200 with no credential, re-measured 2026-09-10, 3 774 281 bytes. But the export index now documents a NEWER surface, `threatfox-api.abuse.ch/v2/files/exports/<AUTH-KEY>/full.csv.zip`, which puts the key IN THE URL PATH. Nothing here uses it. The 2026-09-03 correction was about the endpoint the loader fetches and is still right about it.

AN `urllib.error.HTTPError` IS ALSO AN OPEN RESPONSE, and it stays open for as long as the exception it is chained to. Under `filterwarnings = ["error"]` that surfaces as a `PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning` about an unclosed socket, at an unrelated test, some time after the one that leaked it. `refused.close()` before raising is the fix; `helena.agents` has the same shape and has not hit it only because its exceptions are not held across tests.
failed_approaches: A LITERAL `https://` IN `helena/providers.py`. `tests/test_broker.py::test_no_module_in_the_package_holds_a_broker_address` sweeps EVERY module in the package for an address-shaped literal and its regex includes a scheme-and-slashes pattern, so `f"https://{host}{path}"` fails the whole suite. Do not weaken that regex or carve an exception into it — the rule is what keeps 'replacing the broker is a configuration change' true. `urlunsplit((SCHEME, host, API_PATH, "", ""))` composes the same URL with no literal and is better code anyway.

GUESSING FALSE-POSITIVE OPERATION NAMES INSTEAD OF READING THE OPERATION SET. Three were tried (`get_fp`, `fp_list`, `false_positives`) and all three answered `unknown_operation` — which is a fine way to CONFIRM an absence the documented operation set already showed, and would have been a terrible way to discover a presence. If a later session goes looking for an abuse.ch FP feed, read the documented operation list and the export index first; the three probes are the corroboration, not the method.

A SINGLE-PASS CLAIM BUILDER THAT COUNTS DROPPED CANDIDATES AS IT GOES. The first draft built claims in the loop and then rebuilt them in a comprehension to attach the final count, so every record was parsed and scope-checked twice and the first set was discarded. Select the in-scope entries first, compute `(returned, dropped)` once, then build — every claim of one answer must carry the SAME two counts, which a streaming count cannot give the earliest claim.
next_session_should_know: Task 39 is the analyst tool loop and it now has a real provider to drive. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE WHOLE TOOL IS ONE CALL: `providers.threatfox_tool(credential=settings.providers.abusech_auth_key, cache=tools.EvidenceCache(connection), send_policy=disclosure.send_policy(), logger=..., redactor=..., timeout_seconds=...)`. Everything provider-specific is DERIVED and not passed — the host from `[send_policy.threatfox] disclosed_to`, the endpoint from `providers.SEARCH_IOC`, the retention from the descriptor's 3 600 s refresh floor — so the loop supplies only `scope=RunScope.of(request)`, `budget=RunBudget.of(request)`, `disclosures=Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy())` and `now`. The tool's name is `lookup_threatfox_search_ioc`. (2) `timeout_seconds` HAS NO DEFAULT AND IT IS NOT THE RUN'S CLOCK. It bounds ONE request; `RunBudget`'s wall clock bounds the analysis and is charged on the same ledger as the model calls. A request that outlives the first is a `timeout` QueryFailure; a run that outlives the second is a `budget_exhausted` ToolRefusal with nothing queried. Pick it from `config/policy.toml`'s `[budgets.analyst] retrieval_seconds` divided by the live-query budget, or say why not. (3) A `no_match` FROM THIS TOOL MAY MEAN TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE COUNTS SAY WHICH. `native_evidence` carries `records_returned` and `records_out_of_scope`: `(0, 0)` is 'the provider listed nothing', `(n, n)` is 'the provider listed n things, none about this indicator' — which happens whenever a wildcard address query hits a URL containing that address. Anything summarising analyst evidence should not flatten those into one sentence. (4) NOTHING PACES CALLS AND THIS MODULE IS WHERE A THROTTLE GOES. `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is self-imposed, no rate-limit header exists to measure against, and the wall clock charges the wait. If you add a sleep, it is in `ThreatFoxHuntingAPI._post` and it costs the run's clock deliberately. (5) THE LIVE TEST IS ONE CALL AND IT ASKS ABOUT AN INDICATOR THIS PROJECT MADE UP. `tests/test_providers.py::test_the_hunting_api_still_answers_the_surface_this_adapter_was_written_against` skips only for `timeout`/`transport_error` and deliberately RAISES for `auth_failed`, `quota_exhausted` and `malformed_response` — the first two mean the credential or the terms changed and the third means the surface did, and none of those may be skipped past. It asserts the surface and never the feed's contents, because the publisher expires IOCs after six months. (6) THE FIXTURES ARE REAL BYTES AND THE SHAPE THEY TEACH IS NOT THE EXPORT'S. `tests/fixtures/threatfox/search_ioc_*.json` are five verbatim answers from 2026-09-10; `tests/fixtures/threatfox/README.md` has the table of what each is for and the five field-name differences from `export.json`. Do not write a sixth from the export's shape. (7) `concept/05` NOW CARRIES THREE DATED CORRECTION BLOCKS FROM THIS SESSION — the query surface, the absent FP list and the measured retrieval confound — plus a bullet about the newer key-in-the-path export endpoint. Editing a concept note is above a session's normal authority and the operator should confirm they stand; the full argument for each is `docs/decisions/0028-the-threatfox-hunting-api.md`, which is the source record and was written before the adapter.
